fields.meta_title: Electrician Landing Page for Installs and Repairs | Emergent
fields.meta_description: An electrician landing page that routes EV charger and generator quotes, prices small jobs, and sorts property manager calls. See four examples.
fields.h1: Build an Electrician Landing Page for Installs and Repairs
fields.hero_description: Get an electrician landing page that sends each install quote and repair call to the right person, saved in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What an Electrician Page Needs to Quote
fields.features_subheading: Each part answers a question the office would ask on the callback. Emergent builds all six from one prompt.
fields.feature_1:
A choice between install and repair

Open with two buttons: Install something new, or Fix something that stopped working. The pick sets the questions that follow, so a dead outlet skips the charger questions.
fields.feature_2:
Panel questions on install quotes

Ask for the panel's amp rating and the year the house was built, with Not sure as an answer. The estimator reads both and knows whether to price by phone or book a visit.
fields.feature_3:
Flat prices for the small jobs

List a fixed price for work you quote the same way every time, such as a ceiling fan or a dimmer switch. The page adds up the picks, so the total is known before a visit.
fields.feature_4:
Your license number by the company name

Print the license number and the insurance carrier in the header, where a homeowner reads them before typing an address. Then list the towns you cover on the same line.
fields.feature_5:
A row for every request

Each request is saved to a database you own, with the job type, the panel answers, and the time it came in. The office marks a row Called, then Booked, from the same list.
fields.feature_6:
Alerts and reminders for the estimator

Send each new request to the estimator who prices that job, by email or in Slack. A reminder follows when a request sits without a call for the number of days you set.
fields.why_description: Describe your jobs and who prices each, and Emergent builds the page with its database. Paid plans include code export to GitHub.

fields.tab_content_1:
Ewald sees every 100-amp panel before quoting

Camphor Ridge Electric will not price a charger on a panel it has not seen. Its quote form asks for the amp rating first, and a home with a 100-amp panel goes to Ewald Tarver, the estimator, for a site visit. Everyone else picks an install date. This month 31 requests came in: 9 went to Ewald, and 22 picked a date.
fields.tab_content_2:
Unanswered for 2 days means a reminder to Rukmini

Solvang Electric gives every standby generator quote one owner: Rukmini Ferrell, the estimator. Each request lands on her list, and any request she has not marked Called after 2 days sends her a reminder by email. This month 26 requests came in: 21 got a call in time, and 5 set off a reminder.
fields.tab_content_3:
The price for 2 fans and 3 dimmers: $615

Drystone Electric prints its small-job prices: $165 to install a ceiling fan and $95 for a dimmer switch. The visitor picks how many of each, the page adds them up, and the booking row saves the total. Last week one homeowner picked 2 fans and 3 dimmers and saw $615 before booking a visit.
fields.tab_content_4:
Property managers on contract: 12 of 19 requests

Fennwick Electrical serves 14 buildings under contract, and its form asks property managers for the building and unit number. A building on the list sends the request to Ilsa Madrigal, and any other address goes to the homeowner desk. This week 19 requests came in: 12 from contract buildings and 7 from everyone else.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Electrician Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to an electrician landing page that sorts install quotes from repairs and sends each one to the person who prices it.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Name the jobs you want more of
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask about the panel on installs
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Post flat prices where you have them
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Make the number tap to call
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick the work you want the page to bring in, such as EV chargers, generators, or panel upgrades, and give each its own page if each has its own ads. A visitor looking for a charger price should not read about rewiring.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Keep the amp rating and the age of the house on install pages only. On the repair form they slow down someone whose breaker keeps tripping and who wants a call back today, not a list of questions.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Show a fixed price for jobs you quote the same way each time, and say what the price covers. For anything that needs a look first, say that a visit comes before the number. Nobody then waits on a price by email.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put the phone number in a link a thumb can reach, and tag the form's phone field with the tel autocomplete token. MDN describes that token as a full telephone number, including the country code.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Mark the page up as an electrician
fields.howto_step_5_des: Add LocalBusiness structured data with the business name and phone number, plus your hours. Google's guide says to use the most specific LocalBusiness sub-type possible. Look up the type that names your trade on schema.org.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Decide who hears about each request
fields.howto_step_6_des: Write down which estimator prices which job and how many days a request may wait before a reminder goes out. Put both in the prompt, and the routing and the reminder are built with the page.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Build it and send a test request
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe the jobs and who gets each request, and Emergent builds the page from that prompt. Send a test request from a phone, then check the row in your database and the alert to the estimator.

faq_plan.q: What is an electrician landing page?
faq_plan.a: An electrician landing page is a standalone page built to get one kind of electrical job request, such as an EV charger quote or a repair visit. Its visitors arrive from an ad or a search result. It holds one form and a phone number, with no menu pulling the visitor elsewhere on the site.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an electrician landing page?
faq_plan.a: Pick the job the page should bring in and the questions the estimator needs answered. Then describe both to Emergent's AI landing page builder, with the name of whoever prices that job. Emergent builds the page and the form from that prompt, and you change any part of it by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: What should an electrician landing page ask before quoting a home charger install?
faq_plan.a: Ask where the charger will go and how far that spot is from the panel, and allow Not sure on both. Add the charger model if the homeowner has already bought one. With those answers, the estimator can tell whether a phone quote will hold or a visit has to come first.

faq_plan.q: Can an electrician landing page show flat prices for small jobs?
faq_plan.a: Yes: list a fixed price for each job whose price never changes, and say what it includes, such as parts and hauling away the old fixture. A pest control landing page does the same with plan prices set by home size. Leave anything that depends on the wiring behind a wall to a visit.

faq_plan.q: What should an electrician landing page show to prove the work is licensed and insured?
faq_plan.a: Show the license number exactly as it reads on the license, and the name of your insurance carrier, near the top of the page. Add photos of your own crew and vans instead of stock images. Skip badges you cannot back with a document a homeowner could ask to see.

faq_plan.q: How should an electrician landing page handle repair calls that cannot wait?
faq_plan.a: Put the phone number above the form on the repair page, with the hours someone answers it. Add an urgent choice to the form, such as power out to part of the house, and have it go to the electrician on call that day. The app Emergent builds can send that alert by email or in Slack.

faq_plan.q: Can an electrician landing page also take plumbing calls?
faq_plan.a: It can, but give each trade its own page if each runs its own ads. A plumber landing page asks about leaks and arrival windows, and an electrical form asks about panels and fixtures. One form holding both makes every visitor scroll past questions that are not about their job.

faq_plan.q: What should an electrician landing page promise about callback times?
faq_plan.a: Promise a window you can keep every week, such as one business day, and print it on the screen that appears after the form is sent. Then hold to it: a reminder to the estimator, by email or in Slack, can go out when a request waits past that window.

faq_plan.q: Should commercial work get its own electrician landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you bid it differently. A property manager asks about a building and a contract rate, while a homeowner asks about one room. Give the commercial page its own form and its own owner. Emergent builds the second page from a prompt, and its requests sit in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Should an electrician landing page let customers book a time?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for jobs with a known length, such as a fan install or an outlet repair, and no for quotes that need a look first. Offer a morning or an afternoon visit instead of an exact hour. A roofing landing page books inspections the same way, with the homeowner picking Morning or Afternoon.

plan.angle: The electrician landing page SERP has no Semrush top 10, and the pages that show up for the term are template galleries and design roundups that stop at how the page looks. This page shows four electrician landing pages built around what happens to a request after the click (an EV charger quote that sends 100-amp panels to a site visit, a generator quote that reminds the estimator after 2 days, a flat price list for fans and dimmers, and property manager requests routed by building), each with the form, the routing and the database row behind it, then gives seven build steps an electrical contractor can follow. It makes no code, licensing, permit, safety or load-calculation claims. HVAC, plumber, roofing, pest control and contractor pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build an Electrician Landing Page for Installs and Repairs' and hero 'Get an electrician landing page that sends each install quote and repair call to the right person, saved in a database you own.' cover the whole job; howto_description is one sentence naming what the steps achieve.

intent.evidence: Meta promises four examples (EV charger, generator, small jobs, property managers); all four tabs deliver them with form, routing and database row, plus 7 trade-specific steps (panel questions, tel autocomplete, LocalBusiness markup).

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout: 'panel's amp rating and the year the house was built', '$165 to install a ceiling fan and $95 for a dimmer switch', 'building and unit number'.

openers.evidence: Every feature body opens on a full imperative or declarative sentence: 'Open with two buttons', 'Ask for the panel's amp rating', 'List a fixed price', 'Print the license number'.

craft.evidence: QC Q5 shows two ', so' endings (feature_1, feature_3), under the limit; sentences short and varied, e.g. 'Everyone else picks an install date.'

voice.evidence: Concrete, unglamorous detail reads as operator-written: 'Camphor Ridge Electric will not price a charger on a panel it has not seen.'

truth.evidence: claims_used prompt-build, database-owned, alerts ('by email or in Slack' within 'Slack, email and in-app alerts, reminders and escalations'), code-export ('Paid plans include code export to GitHub'); MDN and Google quotes match domain_sources spans verbatim; sibling references checked against their specs (pest-control 'Plan prices by home size', plumber arrival windows and leaks, roofing 'Morning or Afternoon'); tab sums 9+22=31, 21+5=26, 2x165+3x95=615, 12+7=19.

distinct.evidence: Own stories (panel-gated charger quotes, generator reminders, fan/dimmer price list, contract buildings); sibling primaries appear only as FAQ link anchors, never in headings.
